purpose: Teach: 焼きそば/シチュー/ヘルシー/試飲/薄め/ふき/アサヒ/お中元

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、屋台の、絶対、焼きそば、絶対、好きだったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran, do you remember? When your father was young, he was absolutely crazy about stall yakisoba. Seriously.
lines.style: Gentle opening, as if arriving at a remembered moment. Warm and slightly wistful tone. Deliberate pacing—savoring the memory. Slight pause before the confirmation, inviting her in.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさんの、絶対、シチュー、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、大好きだったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Mm-hmm. And your grandfather loved my stew so much when he was young, didn't he? You remember, don't you, dear?
lines.style: Soft, pleased recollection. Voice opens gently on the affirmation. Tender rhythm—not hurried. The 'dear' lands warmly, as if she's speaking to him across decades of shared history.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、健康のため、絶対、ヘルシー、絶対、な、絶対、お料理、絶対、好んだぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: And when your father was young, he really preferred healthy dishes—all for his health, you know. You remember that, don't you, gran?
lines.style: A light teasing lilt under the wistfulness. Slight emphasis on 'healthy'—gentle irony in the voice. Measured delivery, as if testing whether she remembers this particular detail.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、お酒の、絶対、試飲、絶対、よく、絶対、参加したわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Oh yes—your grandfather used to attend sake tastings all the time when he was younger. Don't you remember, dear?
lines.style: Warm knowing laughter beneath the surface. Voice brightens slightly on 'sake tastings.' Tender but with a hint of gentle conspiracy—as if they're both in on a shared, loving secret.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、お味噌汁、絶対、薄め、絶対、お祖父ちゃんに、絶対、合わせたわよな、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: And your grandmother, you know—she'd always make the miso soup a little lighter, just the way your grandfather liked it. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Soft reflection. Gentle, almost reverent tone—honoring the small act of care. Slower pace on the detail about adjusting the broth. Voice carries quiet affection.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お庭の、絶対、ふき、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、よく、絶対、煮たわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I did. I used to cook butterbur from the garden quite often, didn't I? Do you remember, dear?
lines.style: Pleased remembrance. Voice warms on 'butterbur'—a small pride in the domestic memory. Conversational and present, as if she's right there in that kitchen again.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、アサヒ、絶対、ビール、絶対、毎晩、絶対、飲んだぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: And your father—when he was younger, he drank Asahi beer every single night. You remember that, don't you, gran?
lines.style: Wistful and gently insistent. Slight emphasis on 'every night'—affectionate observation. Slower, almost meditative pace, as if confirming a beloved habit.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、お得意様への、絶対、お中元、絶対、選んでいたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Oh, that's right. Your grandfather was so thoughtful about selecting year-end gifts for his valued customers back then. Don't you remember, dear?
lines.style: Warm, approving recollection. Voice carries quiet admiration for his care and attention. Gentle, present pacing. The closing 'dear' feels intimate and sure.
